correctness.rationale: For any invariant binary process, define the shift-covariant past conditional probability \(p_t\). The explicit conditional maximal coupling to a fair bit has iid fair output (conditional fair given the strict joint past), invariant joint law, and mismatch \(\mathbb E|p_0-1/2|\). The entropy-rate identity \(h=\mathbb E H_{\mathrm b}(p_0)\) and binary entropy concavity give \(h\le H_{\mathrm b}(1/2-\mathbb E|p_0-1/2|)\), leading by inverse-branch monotonicity to the inequality. For each entropy \(s\), the iid bias \(H_{\mathrm b}^{-1}(s)\) has entropy \(s\), the one-site total variation lower bound \(1/2-p\), and a matching coordinatewise iid joining. Both entropy endpoints and one-sided natural extensions are checked; no finite experiment was used.

value.rationale: Provides the exact natural supremum of Ornstein distance at each entropy rate for all invariant binary processes; it is not a mere constant improvement or a single parametric example. The optimal nonlinear envelope is uniform over arbitrary stationary dependence/nonergodicity and realized by ergodic iid measures at every level, giving a sharp quantitative boundary to the new general effective-uniqueness theorem without claiming to solve larger-alphabet/SFT cases.
